child.family_role_pattern: extended family members help with care

parent.family_role_pattern: extended family members help with care

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about how you and your family have been. I will ask about several areas. I will ask about how you've felt physically and your feelings. I will ask about school and friends. I will also ask about information about sleep or taking medicine. We will make a summary of your responses to share with your medical team. Your team is your doctors and your nurses. It is also other people who work with you here. I'll just call them your care team. The things you tell us help the care team to know how to help you. If you ever need to share something urgent or that can't wait, make sure you call your care team right away, or have your family help you call.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how you've felt physically. Have you had any problems with pain? What about sleep? What about nausea? What about your energy level?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Not really. I threw up a lot the first week and then it stopped.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Now I want to ask about your feelings. Have you felt sad, worried, grumpy, or lonely? Have you felt different from usual?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No. I'm okay.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: How is schoolwork going? Have you been able to stay in touch with your friends? How are those things going?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The work is fine. Everybody keeps asking me why my hair looks different and I still don't know what to say. Two girls were whispering about me in the line.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that you don't know what to say when kids ask about your hair. Anything else you want to tell me?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. My mom is tired all the time now. She fell asleep sitting up in the chair and I didn't wake her up.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that your mom is tired all the time. Have you had any difficulties with taking medicine, sleeping, eating, or using the bathroom regularly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My medicine, kind of. We ran out and had to wait two days for the refill, so I didn't get the night ones.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Anything else that you would like to share?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No. I can't think of anything else.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Okay, thanks for sharing all of that information. Now, I will make a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. I'm going to give everything a number. You can just let me know which numbers are most important. We can make them bold and put them at the top of the list. Okay, here's your list:
1. Not knowing what to say to kids at school
2. How tired Mom is
3. Waiting on the refill for the night medicine
Which ones should we put on the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: 2. My mom.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Here's your list:
1. How tired Mom is
2. Not knowing what to say to kids at school
3. Waiting on the refill for the night medicine
Any changes?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. Leave Mom on top.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thanks for talking with me today. I hope your conversation with the medical team will help. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.
—
If anything urgent comes up between visits, make sure you call your care team right away. Your parent can help, if needed.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some specific questions about how you and your family are doing. I will ask about problems in a number of areas. I will ask about your child's physical health, how you are doing emotionally, family and social things, practical things, and how things are communicated with you and your child. We will share a summary of your responses with the medical team. We hope that this process will help with communication and ensuring access to resources. The medical team is your doctors and your nurses. They can address things and offer referrals and support services as needed. This also gives us information about how these services may be working for you. Then we know what we may need to change. If you ever have urgent or time-sensitive concerns between visits, make sure that you call your care team directly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how your child is doing physically. Have they had any problems with pain, sleep, appetite, or side effects of treatment?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nothing to report this week. The nausea settled once they started giving the Zofran ahead of the infusion, and he has more energy in him than he did at the start.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about how you and your family are doing emotionally. Are you noticing any problems with worry, sadness, anger or irritability? What about difficulty focusing? Or not feeling like yourself? Either for yourself or other family members.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're doing all right at home. I'm short on sleep, but that comes with where we are, and it isn't something I'd put on a list for myself.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about family and social relationships. This is about you and your family. How are siblings doing? What about family conflict? What about social support from your family and community? Okay, how have family relationships and communication been? Any specific concerns?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mother is carrying too much of it. She moved in with us the week he was diagnosed, she's up with him at night, and she does the driving on the days I can't. She's exhausted and she'd deny it if you asked her.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Got it, thank you. Anything else about that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, one more thing — school. The kids have started in on him about his hair, and the questions follow him home; he won't let me walk him in from the car now. I emailed his teacher two weeks ago and I've had nothing back.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about day-to-day activities. These are the activities involved with managing your family and your child's treatment. Are you having any difficulty with finances? What about child-care? What about transportation to the hospital or clinic?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He went two evenings without his dex this cycle. The first prescription ran out before I understood I was supposed to ask for the refill ahead of the last dose, and it took two days to get a new one filled. The bills hold up and my mother fills the gaps. I want to know how to keep that from happening at the end of this cycle.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Got it, thank you. Anything else about that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Food, then. He can't eat anything before the Thursday sedation, and he's ravenous on the dex, so we have the same argument every Thursday before we leave.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Finally, I would like to ask about how your care team shares information with you and your child. Do you have any concerns about how much detail you get? What about who gives you the information, or who is in the room for conversations?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much detail, yes. It comes at me all at once in the room and I've stopped taking any of it in. I'd rather have it in smaller pieces.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Any other items to add before I share your summary?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mother, again. Most of this has landed on her, and I'd rather the team heard it from me than from her.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
I have made a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. Here's the summary:
1. The amount of care that lands on her
2. Questions from kids at school about his hair
3. Getting the refill in time
4. Food he can't eat before sedation
5. How much information comes at once
Any of those you would like to put at the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Everything is landing on her, so put my mother first. The questions the kids ask him come next, and the pharmacy after that.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Okay, here is your updated list.
1. The amount of care that lands on her
2. Questions from kids at school about his hair
3. Getting the refill in time
4. Food he can't eat before sedation
5. How much information comes at once
Anything else?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes. In that order, please.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thank you for sharing all of this with me. We hope this list is helpful for your discussion with the medical team. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.
—
If anything urgent or time-sensitive comes up between visits, please call your care team directly.
